thread:
Maya (partnerships): Partner Y flagged a ~7% delta between their portal and our marketplace month-to-date for April. They say their portal shows 1,120,000 tokens and our metering shows 1,200,000. Can we triage?
Diego (partner-success): Partner says they changed their internal unit mapping on 2026-04-05 from 'compute-seconds -> tokens' multiplier 0.8 to 0.75. Their portal applies the new multiplier retroactively to month view but webhook events still contain raw compute_seconds. Could be a conversion mismatch.
Evan (finance): If their portal retroactively reinterprets stored raw numbers, that would explain part of the delta. We need the raw partner CSV for Apr 1-10 and our ingested raw_event records.
Linh (eng-platform): two things to check: (1) timezone/day cutover differences: partner portal is PST, marketplace aggregates in UTC day windows; (2) we apply multiplier at ingestion time using the multiplier value present in our mapping table then. If multiplier changed at partner side after the fact, portal and us will disagree unless partner reprocessed their historical events.
billing-bot: usage_export_ready s3://redwood-metering/partnerY/recon/2026-04-01_04-10/ partner_csv.csv.gz
Nora (ops): I pulled their export. small sample: ```csv
external_customer,ts_local,compute_seconds,multiplier_applied,portal_tokens
cust-101,2026-04-05T23:58:12-08:00,120,0.75,90
cust-101,2026-04-06T00:01:05-08:00,60,0.75,45
```
Diego (partner-success): see the midnight boundary in PST — some of our UTC-day aggregates will put the Apr 6 00:01 PST row into Apr 6 UTC but partner portal groups it as Apr 5 local-day in their UI.
Maya (partnerships): so two orthogonal issues: unit conversion drift + day-window mismatch. Prioritize which to fix first?
Evan (finance): unit conversion affects dollars directly. that's the priority for credits. timezone mismatch affects reporting buckets but not net tokens over a long window. we should compute both though.
Linh (eng-platform): linchpin SQLs I'm running: ```sql
-- tokens we stored (UTC day)
SELECT date_trunc('day', received_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') as utc_day, sum(tokens) FROM marketplace_usage_events
WHERE received_at BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-04-10' GROUP BY utc_day;
-- convert partner raw compute_seconds to tokens using partner-reported multiplier
-- partner local day aggregation (PST)
SELECT (ts_local AT TIME ZONE 'PST')::date as partner_day, sum(compute_seconds * 0.75) as partner_tokens FROM partner_csv_table
WHERE ts_local BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-04-10' GROUP BY partner_day;
```
Nora (ops): I've loaded partner CSV to a temp table at partner_recon.partnerY_apr1_10.
billing-bot: reconciliation_job started by Linh at 2026-04-10T21:34:10Z
Linh (eng-platform): initial numbers: our UTC-aggregated tokens 1,201,320 vs partner portal tokens 1,119,900. If I re-run our aggregates but convert partner compute_seconds with their new multiplier 0.75 applied at ingestion time, our ingested tokens would be lower by ~85k tokens.
Evan (finance): 85k tokens * $0.00012/token = $10.20. confirm invoice impact and whether rounding / scaling in downstream billing could amplify.
Diego (partner-success): partner confirms they didn't reprocess historical webhook payloads when they changed multiplier. their portal retroactively recalculates UI views which confuses comparisons. They offered to provide a reprocessed CSV (apply new multiplier to historical raw compute_seconds) if we need it.
Maya (partnerships): ask them to provide both: (A) the raw compute_seconds extract (no multiplier column), (B) the portal-recomputed CSV. we need to reconcile our raw ingestion + our token conversion logic.
Linh (eng-platform): longer-term fix: store original raw unit (compute_seconds) as first-class field and store any conversion multiplier_version tag. Apply conversion during billing-run using a canonical conversion table that is immutable for closed invoices. That avoids silent retroactive UI changes causing mismatches.
Evan (finance): agreed. in the short term, we should produce a reconciliation file mapping invoice ids -> token delta -> suggested credit. I'll take the suggested-credit draft once Linh posts the final token delta.
billing-bot: reconciliation_job completed. partner_tokens_converted_to_ours: 1,116,500; our_ingested_tokens: 1,201,320; delta: 84,820

Evan (finance): I'll draft credit memo and queue invoice adjustments. need legal cc for >$500 threshold.
Diego (partner-success): Partner will decide reprocess vs credit within 48h.
Linh (eng-platform): RFC note: recommend UTC canonicalization for billing windows, but UI can show partner-local-day with clear note about conversion.
Maya (partnerships): thanks. let's close after credit or reprocess confirmed. keep this thread for the follow-up.
